$comment: How the popup page hands dictated words back to the desktop app (T-1258). The popup is the
console's own page and has no bridge into the app, so, like the island's mood, the result rides
in its document title: ` · typed:<id>:<text>`, the text through encodeURIComponent. The id is
the one the app armed for this press (32 random hex digits, from the OS); a result with any other id, or one that arrives before the
key is let go, is ignored. A null text is `typed:<id>:` -- a tap, silence, a refused voice or a
failed transcription: the app types nothing. `" · "` never appears in an encoded text (a space
is %20), so the segment cannot be cut short or forge a neighbour. jarvis-web's dictation.test.ts
and the app's logic/src/dictation.rs tests both read this table.
